subject: MIMIC Model for DIF testing in lavaan

messages.author: aef1c0bccf05c08b
messages.subject: MIMIC Model for DIF testing in lavaan
parts:
I want to use lavaan to test for differential item functioning using a MIMIC model.  My MIMIC model is shown in the attached image.  The MIMIC model I’m using has one factor regressed on the items, and one group variable (representing two groups) regressed on the one factor.  I’ve provided what I believe to be the correct syntax for implementing this model in lavaan.  Could someone please verify that this is the correct lavaan syntax, or provide me with guidance on how to implement this model in lavaan? 



  model <- 'f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 + y5 + y6 + y7 + y8 + y9 + y10

                  y1 | t1

                  y2 | t2

                  y3 | t3

                  y4 | t4

                  y5 | t5

                  y6 | t6

                  y7 | t7

                  y8 | t8

                  y9 | t9

                  y10 | t10

                  f1 ~ Z'

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: MIMIC Model for DIF testing in lavaan
parts: I want to use lavaan to test for differential item functioning using a MIMIC model.  My MIMIC model is shown in the attached image.

Looks like you want to implement the method from Woods & Grimm (2011).  Unfortunately, that cannot be done in lavaan because they used latent moderated structures to estimated the interaction between the latent trait and the contextual variable.  In lavaan, you would have to use the product-indicator approach, but that is for continuous indicators rather than categorical ones.  You would have to use Mplus, as Woods & Grimm (2011) described and provided syntax for.
Could someone please verify that this is the correct lavaan syntax

Again, you cannot implement their method in lavaan, but there is another problem with your syntax.  Each indicator's thresholds are sequentially numbered within the indicator, not across indicators.  So all of these should be "t1", rather than t1-t10:

y1 | t1

                  y2 | t2

                  y3 | t3

                  y4 | t4

                  y5 | t5

                  y6 | t6

                  y7 | t7

                  y8 | t8

                  y9 | t9

                  y10 | t10

If you want to make your own labels, you can do that the same way other parameters are labeled:

y1 | Th1*t1
y2 | Th*t1

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax2.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: MIMIC Model for DIF testing in lavaan
parts: Is there an lavaan example of the mentioned product-indicator approach for continuous indicators that one could read?

Yes, just published this week:  https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-018-1151-3

We cite a book chapter that include the example lavaan syntax (and simulated data, so you can run the example).  You can contact the first author for a copy.
If the interest is on uniform DIF only, could one just put link(s) between the grouping variable and the continuous indicators and compare the fit between the two models with and without the links?
I don't know what you mean by "put links", but product indicators aren't necessary if you are only testing uniform DIF (i.e., you assume no nonuniform DIF).
How about for categorical indicators?

Product indicators cannot help with that, because we would need to calculate products between the latent item-responses.  If we could do that, we wouldn't need product indicators anyway, because we could calculate the product between the common factor and a contextual variable (e.g., sex or age).
